e.meaning: of the Dorians, an ancient Greek people
e.etymology: From the Dorians, one of the peoples of ancient Greece. Oscar Wilde introduced it as a first name in his 1891 novel The Picture of Dorian Gray.
namesakes: Dorian Gray (title character of Oscar Wilde's novel)

assoc.t: Dorian Gray, Oscar Wilde's ageless portrait sitter
Hurricane Dorian, which devastated the Bahamas in 2019
Dorian mode, a scale in music theory

e.etymology: A modern American coinage in the family of Brayden and Jaylen, blending their sounds.
From the English surname, which comes from the Norman personal name Leodegar (Leger) or from a term for a stonemason. Its use as a first name follows actor Heath Ledger.

assoc.t: actor Heath Ledger
ledger, a book of financial accounts
Ledger hardware wallets for cryptocurrency

e.etymology: From the place name, built from prince and -ton, town. Most Americans know it from Princeton, New Jersey, and its Ivy League university.

assoc.t: Ivy League university and town in New Jersey

e.etymology: From Arabic zayn, beauty or adornment. Zayn is the other common English spelling.

assoc.t: singer Zayn Malik, who performs as Zayn (same sound)

e.etymology: A modern American name, probably the Ja- prefix joined to Amir, in the pattern of Jamar and Jamal.

e.meaning: French feminine form of Marcel, from Marcus, of Mars
e.etymology: The French feminine of Marcel, from Latin Marcellus, a diminutive of Marcus, a name tied to the god Mars. Many Americans know it from Marceline the Vampire Queen in the cartoon Adventure Time.

assoc.t: Marceline the Vampire Queen of Adventure Time
Marceline, Missouri, Walt Disney's boyhood hometown

e.etymology: The Spanish, Italian and Portuguese form of Armand, the French version of Herman, from Germanic hari, army, and man, man.
Shortened from the Scottish surname McKinley, Gaelic Mac Fhionnlaigh, son of Fionnlagh, a name meaning fair hero. It caught on for girls in the 2010s alongside Kinsley and Finley.

From a northern English surname, likely an alteration of Selby, willow farm. Kentucky's first governor, Isaac Shelby, spread it for boys; the character Shelby in the 1989 film Steel Magnolias boosted it for girls.

assoc.t: Shelby Mustang and Cobra performance cars
the Shelby family of Peaky Blinders

e.meaning: pet form of Winifred, from Welsh gwen, fair or blessed
e.etymology: A pet form of Winifred, the English form of Welsh Gwenfrewi, whose first element gwen means fair or blessed. It also shortens Winona and Winston.
namesakes: Winnie Cooper (girl next door in The Wonder Years)

assoc.t: Winnie-the-Pooh, A. A. Milne's honey-loving bear

e.etymology: From Latin Augustinus, a derivative of Augustus, venerable, from augere, to increase. Saint Augustine of Hippo, the theologian who died in 430, made it a lasting Christian name.
namesakes: Saint Augustine of Hippo (early Christian theologian)

assoc.t: St. Augustine, Florida, oldest city in the US
Saint Augustine of Hippo, early Christian theologian

e.etymology: From the English word sincere, from Latin sincerus, pure or genuine. It was rare until rapper Nas played a character named Sincere in the 1998 film Belly, and it reached the US top 1000 for boys in the 2000s.
In use since the 1500s, perhaps first as a pet form of Elizabeth, and long understood as a form of Latin lilium, lily. Lillian with a double l is the more common American spelling.

e.meaning: pet form of Alexander and Alexandra, defender of men
e.etymology: The Russian and Ukrainian pet form of Alexander and Alexandra, from Greek Alexandros, defender of men. In Slavic countries it is used for both boys and girls.
namesakes: Sasha Obama (younger daughter of Barack Obama)

e.etymology: From Arabic Aliya, high or exalted, the feminine form of Ali. Aaliyah and Aliyah are fuller spellings of the same name.
The Ukrainian feminine form of Ivan (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious, by way of Greek Ioanna. It is also popular in Latin America.
e.note: Sounds like I wanna, the setup for joke names such as Ivana Tinkle.

e.etymology: From the Welsh name and surname Trefor, taken from place names built from tref, village or homestead, and mawr, large.
namesakes: Trevor Noah (comedian and former host of The Daily Show)

e.etymology: A phonetic spelling of Margot, the French pet form of Marguerite (Margaret), from Greek margarites, pearl.
namesakes: Margo (eldest sister in the Despicable Me films)

e.etymology: From Old Spanish reyna, queen, the older spelling of reina. Among Catholics it can honor the Virgin Mary as Queen of Heaven.

assoc.t: Reyna, a playable agent in the video game Valorant

e.meaning: small butterfly (Arabic); also a Brazilian water spirit
e.etymology: An Arabic name borrowed from Persian, often glossed as small butterfly. Separately, Yara or Iara is a river spirit in Brazilian Tupi legend, whose name means lady of the water.
A spelling of Oakley, an English place name and surname from Old English ac, oak, and leah, woodland clearing.

assoc.t: Oakley sunglasses (same sound)

e.etymology: The French feminine form of Louis, from the Germanic name Chlodovech (Ludwig), built from elements meaning fame and battle.
namesakes: Louise Belcher (bunny-eared daughter in Bob's Burgers)

assoc.t: Thelma & Louise, the 1991 road movie
Geez Louise, a mild exclamation of surprise
Lake Louise in Banff National Park, Canada
Louise, the bunny-eared kid of Bob's Burgers

e.etymology: From the Scottish clan surname Campbell, Gaelic Caimbeul, from cam, crooked, and beul, mouth.

assoc.t: Campbell's, the canned soup brand

e.etymology: A spelling of Lila, a form of Leila, from Arabic layla, night. The y signals the LY-luh pronunciation.

A fanciful American spelling of Jason, shaped by Jay and Jayce. Jason comes from Greek Iason, linked to iasthai, to heal. It surged around 2013 after rapper The Game, born Jayceon Taylor, used his given name on reality TV.
From Capri, the Italian island in the Bay of Naples. The island's name is usually traced to Latin capreae, goats, or Greek kapros, wild boar.

assoc.t: Italian resort island in the Bay of Naples
capri pants, cropped women's trousers
Capri Sun juice pouches

e.etymology: From an English surname and place name of Old Norse origin, built from the personal name Koli, or kol, charcoal, and byr, settlement.

assoc.t: Colby cheese, a mild orange cheese from Wisconsin
Colby College in Maine

e.etymology: From Hebrew mara, bitter. In the Book of Ruth, Naomi takes the name Mara after her losses. It is also a short form of Maria and Tamara.
namesakes: Mara Wilson (child star of Mrs. Doubtfire and Matilda)

assoc.t: Mara, the demon who tempts the Buddha
mara, Central American Spanish for a street gang (MS-13)

e.note: In Central American Spanish, mara is slang for a street gang, as in Mara Salvatrucha (MS-13).

e.etymology: A recent American respelling of Dream, the word used as a name, with a J in place of the D.
The Spanish form of Alexandra, the feminine of Alexander, from Greek Alexandros, defender of men.
From Arabic zahra, radiant or shining, an epithet of Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad. A closely related Arabic word means flower.
